newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: S.Africa to sign gas deals with Mozambique, Namibia.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa to sign gas deals with Mozambique, Namibia.

text.p: South Africa is expected to sign a gas cross border agreement with Mozambique soon and a similar agreement with Namibia could follow in the near future, Deputy Minerals and Energy Minister Susan Shabangu said on Tuesday.
Shabangu told delegates to a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference that Mozambique's Pande field and Namibia's Kudu field had two of the largest gas reserves in the region.

"We have had a series of negotiations with Mozambique with whom we expect to sign a gas cross border agreement soon. We also expect to sign a similar agreement with Namibia in the near future with the same objectives," she said.
Shabangu said the availability of gas on South Africa's doorstep could see greater regional co-operation.
"Our neighbours cannot develop fully their gas infrastructure unless South Africa participates in the exploitation and utilisation of these resources," she said.
She said South Africa was still hampered by having a strong culture of coal use for energy rather than gas.
"Gas has an important role to play in the development of our Southern African Development Community sub-region. It is a far more environment-friendly form of energy."
South Africa's liquid fuel consumption was growing by about two percent above the economic growth rate as the living standards of the country's population increased.
"These growth trends will require expansion of our refining capacity and or imports of refined products by about the year 2000," she said.
